synthesis.headline: Weigh-In is built and works end to end. v1 is now waiting mostly on Ryan's own time: a handful of hands-on checks and two weeks of real daily use that cannot finish before about 2026-10-19.
synthesis.verdict: The product described in the original design is built and working. Agents flag the calls they make, hooks capture those calls at no model cost, the /weigh-in sitting filters out what does not need you and puts the rest to you as short cards, and every answer is saved as a .kb decision record. The board page, originally planned for slice 2, also shipped. This repository has used Weigh-In on itself to record 14 of your decisions across 8 sittings, so the loop is real and not a demo. The code is in genuinely good shape: all 180 tests pass, there are zero lint findings, the core crate does no I/O as its charter says, and every build decision that affects the code was checked and is in place. v1 is not done yet because it was defined as proof that the product is useful in your daily work, and that proof has not been collected. The two weeks of real use (#23) only open on 2026-10-12. Three surface checks need you at a keyboard: Cowork session identity, the Cowork card, and Windows without Git Bash. You have not reviewed the eval labels. The newest install route, organisation sync, has not been confirmed to reach your machines. The status documents also lag the code: the roadmap still says 0.5.2 and contradicts itself. Few surprises remain on the build side. The real uncertainty is whether the two weeks of use show that people act on what Weigh-In surfaces, rather than dismissing it as noise. The realistic earliest v1 date is around 2026-10-19 to 10-21, and late October is more likely.
synthesis.v1_progress_basis: An equal 50/50 blend of two measures. (1) Planned build deliverables in v1-plan Phases 0 to 4: Phases 1 and 2 are done, Phase 0 is done except the rulesets, Phase 3's build tasks have shipped, and Phase 4 has done only its code review. I put this at about 90%. (2) The seven Phase 3 exit criteria in docs/v1-plan.md:311-324, scoring met as 1 and partial as 0.5: 1 met, 3 partial and 3 not met gives 2.5 of 7, about 36%. Blended: (90 + 36) / 2 ≈ 63%. Counting the evidence-based criteria alone, progress is about 36%. That is the fairer view of how much of v1's proof exists today.

audit.summary: Weigh-In set out to keep a ledger of the questions, assumptions and deferred calls that agents leave behind. Agents mark them at no model cost, hard filters strip out what does not need Ryan, he settles the rest in one short sitting at the end of the chat, and every answer becomes a `.kb` decision record. That whole loop is built and runs today: hook capture, the `/weigh-in` sitting with its five filters and card guards, atoms with commit trailers, and the Artifact board, which was pulled forward from slice 2. This repository uses it on itself, with 14 recorded decisions and 13 `Weigh-In:` trailers in its history. Two things are not yet shown. First, whether the product delivers its promised value: the design's own pass criteria (two weeks of use, at least 60% action rate, at most 10% not-useful dismissals, at least 80% capture precision on labels Ryan has reviewed, one "no decisions need you" sitting) are all unmeasured. Second, Cowork: session identity (V1) and the Cowork question card (V6's Cowork half) have not been checked. Most departures from the original design were recorded properly as decisions. One was not: the board decision to teach Redkiln's kb-ingest the intake keys in slice 1 was quietly moved to slice 3. Some roadmap figures are also stale.

audit.summary:
I found six things the dimensions missed or disagreed on. The most important is the client-repo board guard. wi-7c21e4 is a one-way decision that client items must not reach claude.ai, but the CLI only prints a warning on export. An unreadable config or a client repo that was never initialised falls back to publishing ("artifact" mode). The decision index stops at B-09, the commit-message decision references are incomplete, unattended-run defaults are not measured by any v1 criterion, and the happenstance pin is looser than the docs say. I resolved these conflicts between dimensions:
- Decision count: there are 14 decision records, not 13 (B2 is wrong). 13 is the number of `Weigh-In:` commit references, which name only 12 distinct decisions.
- Eval seed size: the seed has 60 items now (`wc -l eval/seed.jsonl`). The 33 in the tracker's #22 comment is an older figure from before the seed grew.
- Test count: the gate's 31 `#[test]` against 30 integration tests passed is explained by the Windows-only test at `cli.rs:590`, which does not run on Linux. D12's "31 integration" counts that test.
- Unpinned npm install in the release job: this is decided, not open. Record wi-497dc5 ("Leave unpinned", decided by human:ryan on 2026-10-06T04:54Z) supersedes the "open question" wording in E9, B9 and the tracker. C11 is correct.
- Rulesets: E8's evidence (`main` reports protected:true) is stronger than B1's "cannot be confirmed". The v* tag rule is still unverified.

findings.claim: Client repos default to a local board, and their items are never published to claude.ai (wi-7c21e4, a one-way authority decision).
findings.observation:
The guarantee lives only in the skill's wording and one warning; the CLI does not stop an export.
- `board export` still exports when the mode is not `artifact`. It only writes "note: ... do not publish its items to claude.ai" to stderr (main.rs:919-925).
- Local mode is set only when someone runs `init` with `--class client` (main.rs:430-436).
- The defaults are `mode: "artifact"` (env.rs:18-24) and `repo_class: "own"` (env.rs:92). So a client repo that was never initialised publishes.
- A malformed or unreadable config.json silently loads those same defaults (env.rs:106-111, `.ok()...unwrap_or_default()`), and then not even the stderr note appears.
- What remains is SKILL.md:62-67 ("Mode local or off (client repos): never publish").
- D9 noted the silent config fallback only as a risk of splitting the ledger, not as a risk of publishing client items.
- No test covers export or publication behaviour in a client repo.

findings.remaining: Decide whether the CLI should refuse (not just warn) `board export` when the mode is not artifact, and refuse it when config.json exists but does not parse. Add a test for each. Before using Weigh-In on any IQBG client repo, confirm it was initialised with `--class client`.

findings.claim: happenstance is held at 0.3.2, because the ledger's TRUNCATE template and migration step depend on its exact schema (B-01, B-10; roadmap.md:54).
findings.observation:
The hold is enforced only by Cargo.lock and the Dependabot ignore rule.
- Cargo.toml:16-17 declares `version = "0.3.2"`, which Cargo reads as ^0.3.2. A manual `cargo update` would accept any 0.3.x.
- Dependabot ignores `happenstance-*` (.github/dependabot.yml:2,17).
- E9 found that the release build omits `--locked`.
- If a 0.3.x release changed the schema, it could slip in without the migration step B-10 requires. The store fixture tests would probably catch an obvious break, but nothing tests a quiet change to an event payload (D3).
- The source is crates.io only (Cargo.lock:250-267; deny.toml:27-29).
